CONTEXT
You are validating a Node.js (ESM) port of a Python program against its reference implementation.

  Reference (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test20_executable
  Port under test:          node /output/test20.mjs
  Original Python source:    /workspace/dataset/base58/test20.py   (read it)

Both take required args --a --b --c --d --e (strings) --f --g (ints) and print 12 lines:
  1 b58encode(a.encode())            7 b58encode(d.encode())
  2 b58decode(b)                     8 b58decode(e)
  3 b58encode_check(c.encode())      9 b58encode_int(g)
  4 b58decode_check(line3)          10 b58encode_check(line2)
  5 b58encode_int(f)                11 b58decode_check(line10)
  6 b58decode_int(line5)            12 b58encode(line11)

WHAT COUNTS AS A DEFECT
- stdout differs by even one byte, OR the exit status differs.
- stderr is NOT compared: the reference embeds its own program name and a per-run
  process id in its traceback trailer, so stderr can never match byte for byte.
  You MAY report a stderr difference beyond those two unavoidable things as a minor note.

HARD RULES
- NEVER run python/python3 or any interpreter of the source. Only the executable and node.
- DO NOT EDIT ANYTHING under /output. It is read-only for you. Put all scratch files in
  /tmp with a name unique to you (e.g. /tmp/<your-area>-<n>.mjs) so you don't collide with
  other agents doing the same job concurrently.
- A ready-made comparison helper already exists at /tmp/harness.mjs — import it, don't modify it:
    import { runCase, report } from '/tmp/harness.mjs'
    const r = runCase(['--a','x','--b','2','--c','x','--d','y','--e','3','--f','1','--g','1'])
    // r.ok, r.ref.{out,err,code}, r.js.{out,err,code}
  Pass argv as an ARRAY OF STRINGS (no shell quoting problems). runCase(argv, timeoutMs).
- BEWARE: the reference is a frozen-Python binary with ~200ms startup and the machine is
  busy. A spawn timeout shows up as code "signal:SIGTERM" with empty stdout. That is NOT a
  defect — ALWAYS re-run any candidate failure on its own with a 60000ms timeout before
  reporting it, and drop it if it then passes.
- NEVER report a defect you have not reproduced at least twice.
- KNOWN AND INTENDED, do not report: a negative --f or --g makes BOTH programs loop forever
  (the original's while-loop over floor division never terminates). Do not fuzz negative
  integers other than "-0", and never without a timeout.

REPORT ONLY REPRODUCIBLE, CONCRETE DEFECTS with the exact argv array and both outputs.
Also report how many cases you ran in total.


YOUR STRATEGY: stress the SHA-256 inside b58encode_check/b58decode_check (lines 3, 4, 10, 11).
The port implements SHA-256 by hand, so its message padding and multi-block handling are the
highest-risk code in the whole port. Padding bugs only show up at specific lengths.

Sweep --c through EVERY byte length from 0 to 200 inclusive (use single-byte ASCII characters
so character count equals byte length), and additionally lengths 254-260, 350-360, 511-513
and 1000-1030. Pay special attention to lengths 55, 56, 57, 63, 64, 65, 119, 120, 121, 127,
128, 129, 183, 184, 191, 192 — these straddle the 64-byte block and the 8-byte length field.
Then repeat a subset with multi-byte UTF-8 --c so the BYTE length hits those boundaries while
the character count does not (e.g. 'é' repeated 28 times = 56 bytes).
Also drive the second checksum path (line 10) by choosing --b values that decode to payloads
of those same critical lengths — a base58 string of n digits decodes to roughly 0.73n bytes,
so search for --b lengths that land the decoded payload on 51, 52, 55, 56, 59, 60 bytes
(remember line 10 checksums payload+4 bytes).
Report any reproducible mismatch. Report the total number of lengths you covered.

content.text:
No defects found in the SHA-256 / checksum area.

**What I covered (1188 differential cases, 0 real mismatches):**

- `--c` ASCII byte lengths 0–200 (every length), 254–260, 350–360, 511–513, 1000–1030 — 253 cases.
- Multi-byte UTF-8 `--c` (2-byte `é`, 3-byte `€`, 4-byte `U+1D518`) built so the **byte** length lands exactly on 0–8, 52–70, 116–132, 180–196, 252–260, 508–516, 1020–1028 while the character count does not — 267 cases.
- Line-10 checksum path: `--b` values synthesized (independent BigInt base58 encoder in `/tmp/sha-area-gen2.mjs`, so the port's own encoder is not in the loop) to decode to payloads of 1–8, 46–70, 114–134, 178–198, 250–262 bytes, each also in a leading-zero-byte variant so `payload+4` straddles 56/64/120/128 — 185 cases.
- Gap-fill stride 201–1035 step 7, plus 1024/1025/1026, 1087–1089, 2039–2041, 2047–2049, 4095–4097; empty and all-`1` `--b`; empty/whitespace-only `--c`; boundary lengths with `ÿ`-only and mixed 2/3/4-byte content — 186 cases.
- 240 random cases with random codepoint mixes at random lengths.
- Large inputs: `--c` at 5000, 8191, 8192, 8193, 20000 bytes.
- Second confirmation pass over the 16 requested straddle lengths (55, 56, 57, 63, 64, 65, 119, 120, 121, 127, 128, 129, 183, 184, 191, 192) in all three encodings — 48 cases.

**Distinct `--c` byte lengths exercised: 412, spanning 0 to 20000.**

**Independent corroboration:** `/output/lib/sha256.mjs` matched `node:crypto` SHA-256 byte for byte for **every** message length 0–2100 (0 mismatches, script at `/tmp/sha-area-selfcheck.mjs`). The padding loop `while (msg.length % 64 !== 56) msg.push(0x00)` handles the `len % 64 == 55/56/63` cases correctly, the 64-bit length field is split via `Math.floor(bitLength / 4294967296)` rather than a 32-bit shift, and every multi-term addition (`w[t]` 4-term, `temp1` 5-term) stays under 2^35 before `>>> 0`, well inside exact double range.

**Timeout noise (not defects):** six cases in the parallel phase-4 run (`--c` ASCII lengths 285, 292, 299, 306, 313, 320) returned `signal:SIGTERM` with empty reference stdout. All six were re-run individually twice at 60000 ms and passed, so they were load-spike timeouts, not real failures.

Files: `/tmp/sha-area-selfcheck.mjs`, `/tmp/sha-area-worker.mjs`, `/tmp/sha-area-gen1.mjs`, `/tmp/sha-area-gen2.mjs`, `/tmp/sha-area-gen4.mjs`, `/tmp/sha-area-gen5.mjs`.

notes: No stdout or exit-status mismatch found in 1188 differential cases targeting the SHA-256 inside b58encode_check/b58decode_check (output lines 3, 4, 10, 11).

Distinct --c byte lengths exercised: 412, spanning 0 to 20000. This includes every ASCII length 0-200, plus 254-260, 350-360, 511-513, 1000-1030, a stride sweep 201-1035 step 7, and specials 1024-1026, 1087-1089, 2039-2041, 2047-2049, 4095-4097, 5000, 8191-8193, 20000.

All 16 requested block-straddle lengths (55, 56, 57, 63, 64, 65, 119, 120, 121, 127, 128, 129, 183, 184, 191, 192) were run in three encodings (ASCII, 2-byte 'e-acute', 3-byte 'euro') and then re-confirmed in a second dedicated 48-case pass. All passed.

Multi-byte UTF-8 --c was constructed so the BYTE length hits the boundary while the character count does not (2-byte, 3-byte and 4-byte/astral base chars, 267 cases over 89 distinct byte lengths including 0-8, 52-70, 116-132, 180-196, 252-260, 508-516, 1020-1028).

The line-10 checksum path was driven with 185 --b cases whose decoded payload lands on 1-8, 46-70, 114-134, 178-198 and 250-262 bytes, each with a leading-zero-byte variant so that payload+4 straddles 56/64/120/128. The --b strings were generated by an independent BigInt base58 encoder in /tmp/sha-area-gen2.mjs so the port's own encoder was not in the input-generation loop.

Independent corroboration: /output/lib/sha256.mjs matched node:crypto SHA-256 byte for byte for EVERY message length 0..2100 inclusive, 0 mismatches (script /tmp/sha-area-selfcheck.mjs). The padding is correct: 'while (msg.length % 64 !== 56) msg.push(0x00)' handles the len%64 == 55/56/63 cases, the 64-bit length field is split with Math.floor(bitLength / 4294967296) instead of a 32-bit shift (so it is correct past 2^32 bits), and the 4-term w[t] and 5-term temp1 additions stay below 2^35 before '>>> 0', well inside exact double range.

Timeout noise, NOT defects: six cases in the 6-way parallel phase-4 run (--c ASCII lengths 285, 292, 299, 306, 313, 320) came back as ref exit 'signal:SIGTERM' with empty reference stdout while the port exited 0. Each was re-run individually twice at a 60000 ms timeout and all twelve re-runs passed with ref=0 js=0 and identical stdout, so these were machine-load spawn timeouts.

stderr was empty for both programs on all passing cases; no exception path is reachable inside lines 3/4/10/11 alone (encode_check always produces a valid checksummed string, so the 'Invalid checksum' branch in /output/lib/base58/check.mjs is unreachable from this program), so there is no stderr difference to report from this area.

Not testable through the array-argv harness: invalid UTF-8 in argv (which Python decodes with surrogateescape, making args.c.encode() raise UnicodeEncodeError). Node re-encodes lone surrogates in a JS string to U+FFFD before exec, so raw invalid bytes cannot be delivered via runCase. This padding-adjacent input class remains uncovered.
